text:
mike: quick question — planning a small compatibility note for the embeddings endpoint. need to align on how we handle mixed batches (empty strings, nulls, very long inputs), truncation, and what we return for out-of-range batch sizes. cc @sara @jia

sara: short answer: we should be explicit and stable. current runtime does some of this implicitly but clients need guarantees. what are the exact behaviours we want in the v1->v1.1 doc? :thinking:

jia: list of cases we should cover:
- input types (string vs bytes vs array)
- empty string vs zero-length item vs null
- per-item truncation rules and how it's reported
- maximum items per request and expected error code/response shape
- output ordering and presence of placeholders for invalid items

mike: ok here's a proposed contract (please sanity-check):
1) Inputs: request body is { "inputs": [string|null] } only. we will not accept raw bytes in the same endpoint (keep that for future).
2) Empty string ("") is valid — we compute an embedding for it (deterministic vector).
3) null is valid and preserved: we return null in the same position in the embeddings array. we do NOT collapse or reorder.
4) Truncation: we apply per-item truncation at 64k characters (64_000). if an item is longer we truncate and set a top-level response header X-Embeddings-Truncated: true and include per-item annotations in the 'meta' array when ?verbose=true. default is no per-item meta.
5) Batch limits: max_items_per_request = 512. requests >512 -> 413 Payload Too Large with JSON error { "error": "too_many_items", "max_items": 512 }. clients should chunk; we offer an optional streaming/batch helper in SDKs.
6) Output shape: embeddings returned as list same length as inputs. each non-null embedding is Float32 array length depends on model (e.g. redwood-embed-xx = 1536). we include model in response to avoid ambiguity.

tom: I'm worried about point 3. Our current pipeline raises a 400 when payload contains explicit JSON nulls (we had that historically). Changing it to accept nulls will require small changes in the router + perf tests. is it worth it?

jia: accepting nulls is nice for client ergonomics (you can build sparse batches). alternative is to force clients to send empty string for placeholders — but that's ambiguous compared to real empty inputs. preserving nulls makes downstream alignment simpler. implementation: treat null as a short-circuit and emit a null embedding in the returned array without invoking model runner (zero GPU cost).

sara: agree with jia. implement it as a fast-path in request validation. add a small flag in the model runner API so we can bypass scheduling for nulls. also we should update the retro-compat matrix so clients know the change is additive (old clients sending nulls still failed; new behavior is more permissive).

infra-bot: deploy-plan: embed-router-change -> canary -> monitor token-level latency and p95. rollback if model runner queue increases >10% in 5 minutes.

mike: truncation detail — do we want to drop a warning for truncated items in the response body by default? my vote: keep it opt-in (?verbose=true) since it bloats responses for big batches. but we should set a header so infra/observability can detect it without clients changing code.

jia: agreed. header + verbose opt-in is good. also, we should standardize the per-item meta format if verbose: array of same length as inputs with entries null or { "truncated": true, "original_length": 123456 }. that keeps ordering stable.

tom: about output shape: make sure SDKs expose an embedding_length field on model metadata. don't assume all models 1536. otherwise people will try to reshape blindly. also, confirm we return float32 (not float64) to save bytes.

mike: yes float32. and SDKs should marshal to typed arrays. we'll add model metadata: { "model": "redwood-embed-1", "dims": 1536, "dtype": "float32" } in the response.

sara: error semantics for malformed items: if an individual item is an illegal type (e.g., object), we should return 400 with error_type "invalid_input" and not process the whole batch. but we can add a future flag to allow partial success per-item. for now keep it strict to avoid partial processing surprises.

mike: summary action items:
- [jia] add null-pass-through fast-path in router (+ unit tests)
- [tom] update SDK metadata exposure and chunking helper
- [sara] write docs for truncation header + verbose per-item meta format
- [infra-bot] create canary rollout playbook (monitor queue + p95)

jia: quick prototype of expected request/response snippets:
Request:
```json
{
  "inputs": ["short text", null, "", "a...very long..." ]
}
```
Response (verbose=true):
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-1",
  "dims": 1536,
  "dtype": "float32",
  "embeddings": [ [0.001, ...], null, [0.0002, ...], [0.12, ...] ],
  "meta": [ null, null, {"truncated": false, "original_length": 0}, {"truncated": true, "original_length": 250000} ]
}
```

sara: this looks good. one more: when clients hit >512 items and get 413 we should include a hint header X-Max-Items: 512 so clients can auto-chunk. add that to the API error response.

mike: agreed. i'll update the API doc and open a PR that wires these behaviors into the router spec. tagging this thread for async review. if no objections by EOD tomorrow we'll ship the doc and start work. :thumbsup:

tom: small note — add a test that mixes unicode normalization (NFC vs NFD) to ensure truncation is done on codepoints/characters consistently.

mike: good call. will add to test matrix.

sara: thanks everyone, will pull this into the docs PR and ping for final signoff.

infra-bot: created ticket INF-8234 for canary rollout playbook and monitoring alarms.
